# Offline test fixtures

These fixtures contain synthetic inputs and reference outputs produced from those
synthetic inputs. They contain no downloaded firmware, vendor model assets,
guitar captures or factory presets. They also do not contain the Linux
`line6_variax_process_message` reference bytes. Those bytes are compiled
GPL-2.0-only kernel code at `[0x160, 0x240)` in `src/linux_variax_prefix.rs`,
with the notice under `third_party/`. The prefix test feeds them synthetic
message buffers.

- `editor-preset.vwm`: synthetic minimal Workbench-format preset named Synthetic.
- `synthetic-l6ff-python.bin`: 390-byte synthetic FORM/L6FF container. Its image is `bytes(range(256))` repeated four times, not a product firmware file. The Python inspector rejects all 390 prefixes and six damaged fields of this layout.
- `native-body-definition.bin`: generated values across the recovered body schema.
- `native-pickup-definition.bin`: generated electrical/geometry values.
- `native-pack-input.bin`, `native-pack-output.bin`: deterministic synthetic words
  and the original native packer's output for those words.
- `native-resonator-vectors.txt`: finite synthetic boundary values and native outputs.
- `native-body-normalization.txt`: synthetic pickup-position inputs and native float32 results.
- `native-body-interpolation-plans.txt`: synthetic mode/coordinate inputs and traced native routing trees; per-field blending is deliberately bypassed.
- `original-java-word-encoding.txt`: synthetic integer inputs and Java encoder results.

Reference scripts under `scripts/verify_*` document generation and verification.
Ordinary preset, DSP, and file tests use these fixtures and do not need vendor
files or hardware. The Variax prefix test additionally uses the Linux reference
bytes named above. Full original-library reference tests require separately obtained local
vendor artifacts and the ignored analysis/tool directories. See the
[fresh-workspace recipe and validation limits](../../docs/reproducing-references.md)
for hash-checked extraction and reference regeneration. The runner rejects any
fixture digest change; generated expectations are never promoted automatically.

- `native-body-interpolation-input.bin`: six generated variants varying all sections, with safe in-memory coil counts and artificial boundary values.
- `native-body-interpolated-cases.txt`, `native-body-interpolated-output.bin`: 84 synthetic routing/direct-blending cases and complete original-machine-code outputs; no vendor bodies are embedded.

- `native-pickup-combinations.txt`: 128 synthetic raw electrical pairings and original-machine-code float64 output bits/active flags, including IEEE arithmetic edge cases.

- `native-pickup-response.txt`: 540 synthetic complex-transfer/primary-fit inputs and exact original-instruction outputs across varied wiring; no vendor definitions.

`native-pickup-biquad.txt` contains 900 synthetic bandpass/float32 response vectors;
`native-pickup-secondary.txt` contains 24 synthetic residual-fit vectors;
`native-pickup-tables.txt` contains 32 complete 64-double tables;
`native-pickup-calculated.txt` contains 16 sets of 83 assigned response fields.
All use synthetic circuit/control data and original instructions with the
initialized v2 private-runtime/host-libm adapters. No bundled definitions, user
presets, or hardware captures are included. See `scripts/verify_pickup_*.py` and
`docs/pickup-response.md` for scope and limits.

Pickup geometry fixtures: `native-body-pole-offsets.txt` (nine synthetic body
outputs), `native-pickup-projection.txt` (120 synthetic inputs and 61 traced setter
values each), and `native-pickup-placement.txt` (48 unique synthetic placements).
`native-pickup-levels-observed.txt` holds 216 electric level/trim cases; the literal
`unobserved` marks the inactive second level, never a fabricated native output.
`native-pickup-tables-wiring.txt` and `native-pickup-calculated-wiring.txt` add
32 tables and 64 calculated responses for varied synthetic loads and rates.
All are generated by the correspondingly named offline verifier scripts.

`native-vx-float.txt` records 1,012 original bit encodings, including arbitrary IEEE
patterns. `native-dsp-scalar.txt` records 297 scalar-setter cases with native changed
words against seeded 1,091-word arrays. Tests reconstruct the whole initial state
and compare every word, including neighbors. Generated by `verify_dsp_scalar.py`.

`native-dsp-scalar-v2.txt` extends the scalar corpus to 315 cases and includes
six-band EQ count capacity (the prior v1 fixture is historical).
`native-dsp-tables.txt` and `native-dsp-coefficients.txt` contain 927 and 1,218
full-word writer cases. `native-dsp-pickup-blocks.txt` has 360 geometry and
960 response block cases. `native-dsp-simple-blocks-v2.txt` has 1,008 preparation/
assembly cases for six further blocks, with separate microphone parameter and
prepared-field paths. Every snapshot/input is synthetic; original instruction
outputs are recorded with the disclosed host-libm/private-runtime adapters where
needed. Assertions include all 1,091 words, not only changed fields.

`native-dsp-biquad.txt` contains 600 original generic-helper outputs.
`native-dsp-filter-blocks.txt` contains 864 complete low-cut/pick-filter/compressor/
reverb cases, with synthetic parameters and all native word mutations. Reference
helper: `verify_dsp_filters.py`; scope/remaining limits are in `docs/dsp-implementation.md`.


`native-dsp-equalizer.txt` contains 2,304 mixed-precision band coefficient cases.
`native-dsp-eq-blocks.txt` contains 432 complete string/twelve-string EQ cases.
`native-dsp-sitar.txt` contains 288 complete sitar cases, including finite zero-Q
and signed-zero duration inputs. `native-dsp-resonance-blocks.txt` contains 432
body/string-tone cases. All are synthetic numeric snapshots with native outputs.

`native-dsp-body-inputs.bin` is eight independently generated synthetic resources
(17,483 bytes each); `native-dsp-body-outputs.bin` holds their 48 native all-block
outputs (1,091 little-endian u32 words each) in body/variant order. These contain
no vendor model assets. Each input was also validated by the original native
resource serializer. Their default internal rate is 39062.5 Hz. Reference helper:
`verify_dsp_body_variants.py`, generator: `synthetic_dsp_body.py`. Comparisons use
the initialized v2/host-libm reference and do not establish historic libm or audio
parity. No live hardware is used.


Host pipeline fixtures: `original-java-host-pipeline.txt` contains 240 synthetic
logical-parameter cases, original Java native-field mapping, block masks and
complete metadata overlays onto seeded synthetic buffers. `native-dsp-eq-mixing.txt`
adds 300 fractional mixing cases; `native-dsp-derived-sitar.txt` contains 48 seeded
original logical outputs including internally derived frequency NaNs. Public APIs
still reject nonfinite numeric inputs.

`native-host-pickups.bin` contains four independently generated 85-byte pickup
resources, used with the existing eight synthetic body resources.
`native-host-inputs.bin` contains 48 native 192-byte input records;
`native-host-outputs.bin` contains their complete original 3276-byte outputs in
stateful sequence order. `synthetic-host-preset.vwm` and `.packed` provide one
complete original Java-reader/native/Java-overlay result using only those
synthetic resources. The CLI tests compare every byte and verify protected saves.
No original model assets, hardware captures or special vendor tables are embedded.

## Synthetic bank browser fixtures

`synthetic-bank.vwb` and `synthetic-collection.l6c` contain three synthetic banks
with 0, 2 and 3 copies of `synthetic-host-preset.vwm`. Names become `Bank i` and
`Preset i:j` in fixed-width UTF-16 fields. The root contains version-one HEAD and
`JUNK` payload `root unknown`; each bank adds `JUNK` payload `bank unknown!` with
nonzero 0xa7 word padding. `tests/bank_document.rs::bundle` gives the complete
construction recipe and independent expected replacement bytes. They contain
no vendor banks, factory settings or personal captures. Their odd extensions
are Rust preservation/browser fixtures, not original-Java oracle outputs; the
original-Java compatibility corpus uses even extensions (see bank-editor.md).
